policy: CISC architectures lower to C8192; RISC architectures and RISC extensions lower to R8192. ISA-specific decoders must preserve source semantics and lower through canonical MicroOps. This mapping is not a claim of complete instruction coverage or executable native binaries.

chimera-c8192.role: native target for CISC family decoders and semantic lowering

chimera-r8192.role: native target for RISC family decoders and semantic lowering

CISC.reason: Variable-length and operand-rich CISC encodings are decoded by their own ISA frontend, then lowered into the C8192 variable-packet execution model.

RISC.reason: Fixed/mixed-width RISC encodings are decoded by their own ISA frontend, then lowered into the R8192 fixed-64-bit instruction packet execution model.

RISC-extension.reason: An extension is decoded under its owning RISC base ISA and feature profile before canonical lowering.

CISC-extension.reason: An extension is decoded under its owning CISC base ISA and CPU feature profile before canonical lowering.

custom.reason: Project-defined Chimera ISA; preserve its native encoding and execution contract.

EPIC.reason: EPIC bundle and predicate semantics are not equivalent to scalar CISC or RISC decoding.

VLIW.reason: VLIW issue packets and slot constraints require a dedicated frontend.

GPU.reason: GPU machine ISA is generation-specific and must remain on a GPU execution backend.

GPU-VM.reason: GPU virtual IR is not a physical CPU ISA.

VM.reason: Virtual-machine bytecode requires a verifier and sandbox runtime, not a CPU-ISA mapping.

DSP.reason: DSP packet, accumulator, saturation and addressing semantics require a dedicated DSP backend.
